summary: Three full-length passages (886, 854, 910 words) with clear rising difficulty and a proper IELTS mix; all keys are correct. Two T/F/NG items out of passage order have been swapped; the remaining weak point is passage 3 sentence endings that copy the passage word for word.
strengths: Passage 1 completion stems paraphrase the text well ("adjusting the amount of canvas" for "taking cloth in when a gale threatened").
Passage 2 matching people has a fifth person (Priya Raman) who is never the answer, a real distractor.
Passage 3 MCQs and Y/N/NG need the writer's argument (Q29 "Nor need the two be rivals", Q39 "now looks misconceived").

issues.problem: Sentence endings copy the passage: D "return to breed on the shore where they hatched", C "implies that a bird might see the magnetic field" and F "seem to recognise the chemistry of their home water" are near quotes, so Q31, Q33 and Q34 are word matching.
issues.change: Paraphrase the endings, e.g. D "come back to their birthplace to lay eggs", C "suggests the magnetic field may be visible to birds", F "appear to identify their river by its chemical make-up".

issues.problem: T/F/NG order: Q11 (millwrights, paragraph 6) comes before Q12 (the fantail, paragraph 5).
issues.change: Swapped the prompts of Q11 and Q12 in mock6-reading.js (numbers and types kept): Q11 is now the fantail item (TRUE), Q12 the millwrights item (NOT GIVEN); explanation, evidence and paraphrase pair moved with each statement in mock-vocab-A.json.

issues.problem: Summary order: Q18 (water vapour) comes before Q19 (five degrees cooler), but in paragraph B the five-degree figure comes first.
issues.change: Swap the two summary sentences so the five-degree sentence holds gap 18 and the vapour sentence gap 19 (keys swap accordingly).

issues.problem: Passage 2 tests each expert twice (Lindqvist Q19/Q24, Osei Q20/Q26, Whitfield Q21/Q25, Duarte Q22/Q23).
issues.change: Replace one item of each pair, e.g. a summary gap about Raman's "open-crowned species" in narrow streets.
